highlights: Electric quadcopter with an adjustable payload rail and tool-free sensor mounting
Supports optical, multispectral, thermal and lidar payload integrations
Manufacturer quotes 54 minutes maximum flight time; actual duration depends on payload and conditions

The current specifications list 8.5 kg with batteries, 4.2 kg empty and 11.5 kg maximum takeoff mass. The linked handbook printed Rev 1.0 March 2024 lists 8.6 kg, 4.5 kg and 11.6 kg respectively. Configuration/revision differences remain unresolved; case, battery and GS-ONE controller mass are separate.

Manufacturer marketing quotes up to 54 minutes and 3.0 kg payload. No selected source establishes maximum endurance at maximum payload. IP43 is an attributed aircraft rating, not an inspected independent rain test; current -20°C and older handbook -10°C lower operating bounds also remain distinct.

IB388 specifications are per battery: 387.6 Wh, 17 Ah, 22.8 V and 2.08 kg, with 150–300 expected cycles. Capacity and lifecycle are not flight duration. The charging procedure recommends one IB388 per IMARS D300+ and supplies no complete elapsed charge time; 17 A does not prove one-hour charging.

Battery hot swap requires the aircraft to be landed and disarmed, with one battery connected throughout the exchange. A soft reboot reconnects the new batteries without cutting payload power and permits waypoint-mission resumption; this is not an in-flight swap or uninterrupted airborne endurance.

Current documentation specifies Cube Orange+, dual Here4, a LightWare SF000/B sensor, 12 V at 2 A payload power and ArduPilot QUAD V. The older handbook instead names Cube Blue H7 and an 18 V rail. These are source/configuration differences rather than silently interchangeable hardware.

Radio documentation separates an ideal 6 km radio-manufacturer line-of-sight rating from 1.5–2.3 km manufacturer field tests in varied urban environments. Terrain, weather and interference matter; radio reach is neither GNSS accuracy nor proof of permission to fly that distance.

The shop lists eight Herelink/GS-ONE and care variants, from 23,000 USD for Herelink/Foundation to 34,500 USD for GS-ONE/Elite. JSON and JSON-LD availability flags conflict with sold-out/unavailable HTML fallback text, so current stock is unverified. Annual care fees, GS-ONE endurance and accessory prices are separate from aircraft purchase and flight duration.

highlights: Heavy-lift electric multirotor with an open payload architecture
Dovetail payload interface supports sensor changes and an integrated FPV camera supports piloting
Autopilot supports waypoint missions, position hold and return-to-launch

Current physical specifications distinguish 7.8 kg empty, 16.3 kg with batteries and 24.9 kg maximum takeoff mass. The 165.5 × 154 × 76.5 cm flight-ready aircraft folds to 47.5 × 49.5 × 47 cm; the 29 kg transport-case package is separate from aircraft mass.

Payload remains a source discrepancy: current physical table says 8.6 kg / 19 lb, marketing headline 19.1 lb and service-ceiling example 8.7 kg. The shop separately says up to 28.7 lb with appropriate certification. That conditional configuration is not a universal standard payload or independent authorization advice.

Up to 43-minute maximum flight time is a supplier headline, not a maximum-load guarantee. The specification page explicitly requires gimbal plus sensor mass when estimating flight time. The shop’s universal duration-regardless-of-payload wording is not adopted as a measured performance conclusion.

Current flight-stack documentation names Cube Orange+, dual Here3 M8P and Universal Payload Interface 2.1 or 3.0. The linked IF1200A Rev 2.0GB 2023 handbook and January 2023 compliance sheet instead name Cube Blue H7; these documents retain their historical configuration scope.

The January 2023 compliance sheet explicitly says Blue Herelink was NDAA compliant but not approved by DIU for Department of Defense UAS operations. Current Blue UAS/NDAA marketing is an attributed supplier claim; no present complete-aircraft regulatory or procurement certification is independently verified here.

The manufacturer summarizes Tattu per-battery values of 12S1P, 16 Ah, 44.4 V, 710.4 Wh and 4.25 kg ±0.10 kg. TA3200 can charge two batteries simultaneously on independent A/B channels; its 3200 W, up-to-60 A and approximately 6 kg specifications belong to the charger. The charging procedure recommends 16 A but supplies no full elapsed charge time.

The old IF1200A shop URL redirects to the currently titled IF1200 product; the current documentation also uses IF1200A for its interface and linked manual. This supports a family/naming relationship, without inventing a separately available A model or assuming all historical configurations are identical.

Eight listed controller/care variants span 33,500 USD for Herelink/Foundation to 46,000 USD for GS-ONE/Elite. Structured availability flags and rendered sold-out/unavailable fallback disagree, so current stock requires confirmation. Annual service plans, controller battery hours and individual payload sensors are separate from aircraft purchase and flight time.

highlights: Inspired Flight’s timeline states company founding in San Luis Obispo in 2017 and IF750 quadcopter launch in 2018. Current aircraft collection lists medium-lift IF800 TOMCAT and heavy-lift IF1200; this is a selected current portfolio, not proof of complete historical coverage or current stock.

Current IF800 and IF1200 documentation describes modular payload integration, ArduPilot waypoint missions and return-to-launch. Their payload, maximum airborne duration, assembled aircraft mass, takeoff mass and radio range are separate quantities; no source establishes all advertised maxima simultaneously or independently unique advantages.

IF800 current mass, takeoff mass, operating envelope, flight controller and payload rail differ from the linked March 2024 handbook. IF1200 payload figures differ between table, headline and service-ceiling example; older IF1200A manuals/compliance text retain dated configurations. Differences remain visible rather than silently normalized into universal ratings.

Shop prices are listed per controller/care variant: IF800 from 23,000 USD and IF1200 from 33,500 USD for Herelink/Foundation, with other combinations costing more. Public structured availability flags disagree with sold-out/unavailable HTML fallback text. Annual care plans and multi-year bundles are services, not universal aircraft prices or confirmed inventory.

IB388 and Tattu batteries, IMARS/TA chargers, GS-ONE/Herelink controllers, FPV cameras, payload gimbals, imaging/lidar sensors and Inspired Suite software have accessory or software roles. Their masses, battery hours, capacities, dimensions and prices do not become extra aircraft identities or whole-aircraft specifications.

American-made, Blue UAS, NDAA, safety and leadership language remains attributed supplier positioning. The January 2023 IF1200A compliance sheet includes a Blue Herelink Department-of-Defense-operation limitation. No current independent certification, procurement eligibility, operational permission or market/search leadership is established by this selected technical review.
